questions.q: What is the difference between a Timestamp and a Timedelta?
options: A Timestamp is a moment; a Timedelta is a length of time
A Timestamp is a date only; a Timedelta has a time zone
why: Correct. Timestamp minus Timestamp gives a Timedelta.
A Timestamp can hold a time of day too. A Timedelta has no zone.

questions.q: pd.Timestamp('2024-03-10') - pd.Timestamp('2024-03-01') has how many days?
questions.why: From 1 March to 10 March is 9 days.

questions.q: Naive times were recorded in UTC. You want them on Tokyo's clock (UTC+9). Which steps?
why: Correct. Say the data is UTC first, then change the clock.
That would claim the numbers were already Tokyo time, so the real moment is wrong by 9 hours.

questions.q: 12:00 UTC is what clock hour in Tokyo (UTC+9, no DST)?
You sum hourly data per local day in New York. On the spring-forward day the total looks about 4% too low. What is the most likely reason?
options: That local day has only 23 hours
why: Correct. 23 of 24 hours is a drop of about 4%, a shorter day, not a data error.

questions.q: A model uses 'hour of day' as a feature. Timestamps are stored in UTC but customers live in Berlin. What is best?
options: Convert to Europe/Berlin first, then take the hour
Remove the time zone, then take the hour
why: Correct. Customer behavior follows the local clock, including DST changes.
The UTC hour shifts against local life by 1 hour twice a year.
Removing the zone hides the problem and keeps the same shift.

questions.q: Which freq code means one hour in pandas 2.2?
why: Correct. Lowercase 'h' is the current code.
